overall_conclusion: As written, the plan does not make money. Its pricing formula excludes internal labour from cost, so six of the twelve offers carry negative expected margin even under the most favourable assumption of founders on survival wages, including several the plan labels easiest to test immediately. Not one offer passes the plan's own kill rule of RM250 per internal hour; the best is RM240. The plan's own 30-day pass mark of RM15,000 collected is a loss-making month under every staffing scenario, and it was set before the monthly burn was known. The offers with acceptable margin (PC-04, PC-05) have delivery capacity below the units per month needed to cover burn, so they cannot scale to break-even on their own. HDJ's measurement product line sits on a legal boundary that moved against it in October 2024: the Licensed Land Surveyors (Amendment) Act 2024 raised the penalty for a non-licensed party conducting a geomatics survey to RM250,000 and 3 years, and twelve professional bodies state the new definition is unbounded with no implementing guidelines. Separately, the Official Secrets Act 1972 makes taking measurements or surveys within a prohibited place - which includes premises storing petroleum products - punishable by 1 to 14 years, and the target market of factories and warehouses overlaps that set. The plan's discipline is genuinely strong: prepayment, no capex, no fixed headcount, MOU is not revenue, V/S/C/M evidence grading, and L1/L2/L3 accuracy disclaimers are more rigorous than most formal due-diligence frameworks, and they are the reason survival is possible. PC-01 at RM2,500-4,800 carries 39-68% margin at survival wages, has adequate capacity, touches no criminal statute and delivers in 20 internal hours; it is a real starting point. The moat the plan has written down but not recognised is that Malaysian law forces a foreign vendor to route ST COA and MCMC type approval through a local entity - that certificate, not a market map, is the only structural chokehold available to a firm of this size, and it must be sold as a recurring, per-unit, indemnified and insured position rather than a one-off fee. Cut twelve offers to three, compute the burn, and buy back real hour data with the first three engagements before any further commitment.
